h: Play smart, then explore the city
p: Want the best score on the board? Talk to each other. That's the big secret with Immersive Gamebox. Groups that split roles early, with one person on targets, one on puzzles and one calling out the timer, usually do much better than those who all run at the same wall. Wear trainers and comfy clothes, keep bags and coats out of the way, and pay attention to the briefing at the start.

Sessions run for a set length and the games on offer change from time to time, so check what's available before booking. Families with younger players should pick a lighter theme, while teens and adults might fancy something faster and more frantic. Arrive a few minutes early so nobody misses the start.

Once you're done, Liverpool has loads more to see beyond the waterfront. The Walker Art Gallery and World Museum sit side by side on William Brown Street, right next to the grand St George's Hall, and they're great for families on a rainy afternoon. The Mersey Ferry is a classic way to see the skyline from the water, and you might even hear Ferry Cross the Mersey playing as you go.

With more time, head north to Crosby Beach to see Another Place, Antony Gormley's 100 cast-iron figures staring out to sea. It's an unforgettable sight, especially at sunset. Back in town, a bowl of scouse, the stew that gave locals their nickname, is a fitting way to refuel.
